framework: Small-Micro-Cap Stock Research Master Prompt v3.0
name: Hemant Surgical Industries Limited
summary: Hemant Surgical is a medical-distribution and localization scale-up, not an established compounder. FY26 consolidated sales reached ₹231.81 crore and core EBITDA ₹23.22 crore, but reconstructed operating cash flow was negative ₹32.04 crore. Large tender receivables, deposits, demand borrowings and the post-year-end Lifesenz acquisition make cash availability more important than headline earnings growth. gates.name: Integrity and minority protection
gates.rationale: No substantiated severe integrity failure found. Related-party loans and acquisition, capital-raising costs and bank-stock statement differences need scrutiny. Clean opinions and company responses are preserved.
gates.resolution: Obtain the detailed related-party acquisition valuation, consideration destination and minority approval record, plus corrected bank-stock reconciliations.

gates.name: Financial reliability
gates.rationale: Material cash-flow presentation, comparative borrowing classification and bank-stock discrepancies require issuer/auditor reconciliation. This is not a finding of fraud.

gates.rationale: October cash, FD releases, demand-loan renewal and new subsidiary burn are unverified. Conservative conditional paths breach the cash floor; the CRA provides meaningful positive counterevidence.

sections.title: Executive Verdict
sections.text: Hemant Surgical is a medical-distribution and localization scale-up, not an established compounder. FY26 consolidated sales reached ₹231.81 crore and core EBITDA ₹23.22 crore, but reconstructed operating cash flow was negative ₹32.04 crore. Large tender receivables, deposits, demand borrowings and the post-year-end Lifesenz acquisition make cash availability more important than headline earnings growth. At the secondary ₹618.60 close on 19 October 2026, current-share market capitalization is ₹899.30 crore; the official BSE quote and complete trading tape remain unverified. BQS, Growth Quality Score (GQS) and IAS are all NS. Classification: Hold — unresolved; high impairment risk. An auditor-backed cash reconciliation, dated group funding bridge, accepted CMSS terms/collections and attributable plant returns could change the assessment. [S1][S6–S9][M1][M2] The investment type is a working-capital-led expansion/special situation, not a validated high-quality compounder. Medical demand and longstanding product-principal relationships are strengths, but a large order value is not free cash, guaranteed recurring revenue or an automatically valuable manufacturing franchise. No ordinary five-year return or entry price is supportable while current funding is unverified. Separate rescue scenarios are explanatory, not recommendations.

sections.title: Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text:
Hemant Surgical Industries Limited is the exact issuer: CIN L33110MH1989PLC051133, BSE SME code 543916 and ISIN INE0GYI01028. Legal incorporation was 27 March 1989. Marketing references to 1985 origins do not change that date. The HSIL$ interoperability ticker is not the unrelated HSIL/Somany issuer. A conflicting scrip-code typo in an annual-report paragraph does not override the legal identity and exchange master.

The information cutoff is 20 October 2026; sources were accessed on 21 October. The ₹618.60 reference close on 19 October is secondary, not officially authenticated or executable. Current issued capital of 14,537,600 shares implies ₹899.295936 crore market capitalization. Six standalone annual observations cover FY21–FY26; only FY25–FY26 consolidated history is available. The March consolidated perimeter excludes Lifesenz, acquired in June. Accounting is Indian AS, not an assumed Ind AS lease model.

The nominal INR equity hurdle is 15% over 19 October 2026 to 19 October 2031. A ₹5 lakh reference budget buys two 400-share lots: 800 shares costing ₹494,880 before expenses, leaving ₹5,120. Three lots would cost ₹742,320. Confidence is high on identity, issued capital and audited P&L totals; medium on long-term revenue history and cash reconstruction; low on current funding, attributable returns, final tender terms and liquidity. G1 is Conditional; G2, G3 and G4 are Hold — unresolved. Missing evidence alone is not a gate Fail.

Liquidity diagnostics use only twenty secondary observations, not a full official tape. Mean and median close-times-volume proxies are ₹2.6494 crore and ₹1.0499 crore. Continuous 2/5/10% participation estimates of 2.36/0.94/0.47 days are not executable forecasts. Whole-lot daily median capacities are 0/2/4 lots; eleven, one and zero sample days respectively have no capacity for even one lot. At 5% the two-lot median capacity permits an arithmetic one-day fill, but one sample day permits none; spreads, circuit queues and missing sessions can invalidate that illustration. Sixty checked NSE archives have no issuer rows, which does not mean sixty zero-trade BSE days. L remains NS.

sections.title: Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text:
BQS, GQS and IAS are all NS and ineligible for ranking. The factors are GOV 4, MOAT 5, REV 8, DUR 6, CAP NS, CASH 3, BAL NS, EXEC 5 and EARN 6. IAS factors R, D, P and L are NS.

BQS has a known weighted contribution of 4.06 and 80% coverage. Missing CAP and BAL account for 20%; the exact raw bounds are 4.26–6.06. GQS means Growth Quality Score, not governance. Its known contribution is 5.60 with 85% coverage and CAP missing; raw bounds are 5.75–7.10. Persistent CASH 3 applies a cap of 5. The cap-adjusted mathematical bounds of 5–5 do not fill missing CAP or convert NS into a score of 5. IAS has 0% point coverage and independent-factor bounds of 1–10; propagating BQS bounds produces 1.815–9.015, still not a point estimate.

Fixed weights and every contribution are calculated with Decimal strings. No missing factor is renormalized or replaced by a midpoint. REV starts at 9 for a five-year revenue CAGR of 31.0475%, receives no discretionary trajectory adjustment, and is capped at 8 by medium confidence. Three-year growth is a cross-check, not a second score. CAP requires attributable incremental returns, not merely a positive aggregate ratio. The full thirteen-factor audits retain facts, contrary evidence, source IDs and confidence.

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text:
Hemant distributes, assembles/processes and increasingly manufactures medical devices and consumables across renal care, surgical disposables, critical care, radiology/imaging and ophthalmology. Customers include hospitals, diagnostic centres, dealers and doctors; government procurement now adds a much larger tender component. Importing products and servicing customers earns distribution/service margins. Localization can improve value addition only if volumes, approvals and costs cooperate.

Sales are not immediate cash. Inventory and imports, hospital receivables, security deposits and installation or acceptance conditions can consume capital before collection. The annual report describes operations at Achhad, Atgaon, Bhiwandi and Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar, with 109 employees. These are operating assets, not a second property-valuation add-on.

Solar Opto is within March consolidation. Lifesenz became a 66.66%-owned subsidiary on 1 June 2026 and adds different oncology-service/research risks. The acquisition release does not establish clinical efficacy or commercial success. Current product volumes, utilization, customer-cohort margins and geographic revenue splits are insufficient for a precise unit-economics model.

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.text:
The potential advantage is longstanding product-principal relationships, application/service knowledge and local distribution, not monopoly technology. ICRA describes a JMS association exceeding thirty years and exclusive India distribution, while also flagging modest value addition, competition and unhedged foreign exchange. JMS-linked revenue fell from 65% in FY20 to 49% in H1FY26. Diversification is useful but does not by itself prove higher quality. The prospectus reported top-ten customer shares of 40.65%, 39.03% and 33.26% in FY23, FY22 and FY21; current government-customer concentration needs an updated split.

Localization may create process or regulatory advantages, but underlying approvals, utilization and attributable cash returns are not independently verified. Peer comparisons illustrate economics rather than justify a multiple. Poly Medicure reported FY26 consolidated revenue of ₹1,875.26 crore and operating EBITDA of ₹457.70 crore, a 24.41% margin, with acquisitions qualifying growth. Trivitron's provisional FY25 revenue of ₹489.8 crore and 3.9% operating margin illustrate thinner product/distribution economics and reliance on promoter funding. Skanray's 9MFY25 revenue of ₹139.5 crore and −22.5% margin illustrate execution and operating-leverage risk. Different periods, mix, acquisitions and leverage prevent direct valuation transplantation. MOAT 5 recognizes useful relationships without inventing durable pricing power.

sections.title: Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text:
Standalone revenue in FY21–FY26 was ₹59.7646, ₹103.5700, ₹109.1482, ₹105.6075, ₹106.5266 and ₹230.9871 crore. Five-year CAGR is 31.0475% and three-year CAGR 28.3878%; ten-year history is not available. Annual rupee additions were ₹43.8054, ₹5.5782, −₹3.5407, ₹0.9191 and ₹124.4605 crore. A smooth CAGR hides stagnation followed by one exceptionally large jump.

FY26 consolidated revenue was ₹231.8066 crore. No mixed-scope CAGR is used. H1FY26 consolidated revenue of ₹64.6201 crore implies H2 revenue of ₹167.1865 crore, against FY25 H1/H2 figures of ₹48.8706/₹57.7663 crore. H2 is annual minus half-year, not an independently reported quarter. No H1FY27 release was located by the cutoff, so there is no invented October TTM.

Tender execution is a major driver, but price/volume and organic/acquired bridges are unavailable. The February CMSS disclosure totals ₹264.33 crore inclusive of taxes and with commercial terms still being negotiated. It cannot be added in full to already recognized FY26 sales or labeled remaining backlog. Base FY27 revenue of about ₹312.94 crore requires about ₹81.13 crore additional annual sales, supported by accepted orders, repeat distribution and localized production. These are underwriting requirements, not established bookings.

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text:
The plausible runway combines recurring consumables, distribution access and selective localization. Funded growth is the bottleneck. ICRA expected ₹40–50 crore capex across FY27–FY28 and revenue above ₹300 crore in FY27, but these were April forecasts informed partly by March liquidity. The base scenario uses ₹45 crore capex across those years and FY27 growth of 35%, followed by 12%, 12%, 10%, 10% and 8%.

The model pays separately for working capital, operating security deposits, tax, interest and assumed Lifesenz cash burn of ₹0.75 crore per year. Burn is an analyst scenario, not a subsidiary forecast. Deposits are not treated as free investments. Operating invested capital rose from ₹79.36 crore to ₹135.40 crore. Normalized NOPAT gives a 15.15% average ROIC proxy and an 18.72% aggregate incremental proxy, but neither isolates new-plant, government-contract or acquisition returns. CAP remains NS.

GQS remains NS with a CASH 3 cap of 5. Rapid revenue growth is not equivalent to cash-generating growth. Required evidence includes factory capacity, throughput, approvals, utilization, contract cancellations, collections and incremental gross profit. A large healthcare market cannot substitute for an accessible-volume and funding bridge.

sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text:
The business is promoter/family-led with a long operating history. Unmodified statutory and internal-control opinions, no auditor-reported fraud and no declared wilful default are important counterevidence, not proof that every allocation is sound. Note 35 and CARO disclose March stock-statement figures of ₹85.1564 crore submitted to banks versus ₹54.6958 crore in books; September figures were ₹32.1524 crore versus ₹40.7938 crore. Management explains a 25% creditor margin, offsets for LC-margin fixed deposits, and an inventory clerical/human error. The appropriate next step is a corrected bank-return reconciliation, not an unsupported fraud allegation.

The related Lifesenz loan of ₹5.0505 crore lacked a specified repayment period. Auditors could not assess scheduled repayment regularity where no schedule existed and said the terms were not prejudicial. The 1 June completion filing is authenticated; the 9 June issuer release says 66.66% ownership for ₹19.98 crore. The detailed 27 May valuation/transaction annexure was inaccessible. The annual report describes subscription while secondary coverage describes purchase, leaving the consideration destination and treatment of the old loan unresolved. The model conservatively assumes ₹19.998 crore and separately tests ₹19.98 crore; it does not assert that the higher precision is verified. The company describes related-party dealings as ordinary-course and arm's-length.

FY26 issue costs of ₹7.0119 crore against ₹61.52704 crore gross equity/warrant receipts are material. A ₹1.7648 crore deferred-tax credit in premium is not cash. The promises-versus-delivery record is mixed: CMSS's proposed 30 September completion was conditional and is not verified complete; MediTape commissioning and JMS validation are management claims without underlying certificates; January 2027 imaging localization is future; ₹350 crore aggregate tender wins are not unexecuted backlog. A complete primary shareholding/encumbrance record is still required; a truncated PDF or landing page is not that record.

Transaction perimeter matters: if this was a genuine new-share subscription, the consideration could remain inside the consolidated group rather than leave for an outside seller. The full external-use case is therefore conservative, not proof cash left the group. An explicitly optimistic alternative sets external acquisition cash use to zero while retaining subsidiary burn, with no second acquired-cash, loan-recovery or terminal-value add-on. Fungibility to the parent and other subsidiary cash uses remain unverified; ordinary return fields stay null.

sections.title: Financial Forensics
sections.text:
FY26 consolidated PBT of ₹23.5865 crore plus interest of ₹3.9657 crore and depreciation of ₹1.5355 crore, less other income of ₹5.8639 crore, gives core EBITDA of ₹23.2238 crore. Core EBIT is ₹21.6883 crore. The conservative core PAT proxy is (PBT minus all other income) times 75%, or ₹13.29195 crore, versus reported PAT of ₹18.1910 crore. Other income comprises interest ₹1.6656 crore, insurance ₹1.4630 crore, rent ₹0.7102 crore, asset gain ₹1.0400 crore, subsidy ₹0.3735 crore, writebacks ₹0.6078 crore and other receipts ₹0.0038 crore. Recurring rent and interest may have value but are excluded consistently; no second property value is added. FY25 fire insurance and fire loss require net normalization, not a one-sided benefit.

The FY26 cash-flow labels are visibly displaced. Reconstructing operating cash gives ₹26.5033 crore before working capital minus ₹54.1530 crore working-capital absorption minus ₹4.3920 crore tax, or −₹32.0417 crore. Adding investing of −₹2.9746 crore and financing of ₹69.3059 crore reconciles opening cash of ₹9.5469 crore to ₹43.8365 crore. This reconstruction is not a claimed auditor-approved correction. The standalone statement's printed financing of ₹76.3834 crore omits ₹7.0119 crore issue fees relative to corrected ₹69.3715 crore. Its printed cash change of ₹41.3861 crore differs from the balance-sheet increase of ₹34.3742 crore. Both versions remain visible pending an issuer/auditor bridge.

FY25 original CFO included short-term borrowing changes. The later comparative is ₹4.5945 crore standalone and ₹4.6310 crore consolidated, not ₹8.9206/₹8.8404 crore. FY24's later CFO of −₹4.1548 crore differs from original −₹7.5580 crore; FY23 restated and statutory alternatives remain separate. FY26 annual asset purchases of ₹9.3904 crore and sale proceeds of ₹7.2600 crore differ from results lines of ₹1.6486 crore and negative ₹0.4818 crore, although both yield ₹2.1304 crore net asset cash use. Gross capex and FY26 FCF therefore remain NS; net asset use is not known maintenance capex.

Receivables are ₹67.3503 crore, inventory ₹59.0498 crore and payables ₹71.3111 crore. Average DSO is 69.07 days versus a closing-balance proxy of 106.05 days. Inventory days of 104.45 use a COGS proxy; payable days of 103.51 use purchases, yielding an indicative 70.01-day cycle rather than a homogeneous precise measure. Receivables older than six months of ₹7.0430 crore and older than three years of ₹1.2195 crore need collection evidence despite being classified good. ONWC of ₹62.9115 crore includes prepaids once, excludes related loans/customs advances, and is separate from ₹19.0451 crore operating security deposits.

March gross debt is ₹49.6648 crore; core interest cover is 5.47 times and debt/EBITDA 2.14 times. These are not October funding measures. Cash includes ₹38.6126 crore fixed deposits of unverified availability; longer-dated bank deposits of ₹4.9433 crore are excluded. Customs paid under protest of ₹3.5603 crore is neither a new payment nor assumed recoverable cash. Unpaid tax disputes of ₹0.8862 crore are stressed separately. BG interest of ₹2.474 crore, gratuity of ₹0.8363 crore and a property-sale advance of ₹0.7668 crore are retained once as claims. Current shares of 14,537,600 replace historical weighted EPS denominators. Optional exercise of 600,000 remaining warrants adds both ₹8.865 crore and dilution, never the already-received 25% deposit again.

sections.title: Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text:
The secondary ₹618.60 quote and current share count imply market capitalization of ₹899.295936 crore, 49.44 times FY26 reported PAT, 67.66 times normalized core PAT and 7.06 times historical book equity. Using March debt and cash/current accounts only gives an EV/core EBITDA cross-check of 40.64 times, not verified October EV.

The five-year model runs from 19 October 2026 to 19 October 2031, with a separate conditional March-to-entry bridge, remaining FY27 stub, four full fiscal years FY28–FY31 and an FY32 terminal stub. Revenue, EBITDA, depreciation, interest, cash tax, working capital, deposits, capex, debt repayments, shares and cash floors are linked annually. All ordinary IRR and entry fields remain null because current funding is unverified. Every conservative non-rescue path breaches the 2%-of-revenue cash floor, including before entry; peak gaps are ₹44.57 crore bear, ₹39.56 crore base and ₹37.43 crore bull. Their conditional returns and entry prices are also null. Financing-agnostic terminal prices are diagnostics, not valid shareholder returns.

Separate counterfactual rescue cases issue whole shares at a 50% discount to entry with 3% fees. Gross rescue funding of ₹45.94/₹40.78/₹38.58 crore gives bear/base/bull annualized returns of approximately −38.30%/−8.30%/+12.65% to original shares, before trading costs. Even the bull rescue falls short of 15%. These are assumptions, not financing commitments or ordinary fair values. The first rescue is explicitly hypothetical at entry and does not claim a historical issue.

Terminal EV uses 8/12/16 times EBITDA, adds signed cash less the retained operating floor, and subtracts debt and known claims. No IPO residual, operational property, related-loan recovery, acquisition cost or old warrant deposit is added twice. DCF retains operating-cash reinvestment and the signed entry cash deficit. It tests WACC of 12/15/18%, terminal growth of 3/5% and terminal ROIC of 12/16%; unfunded conditional entry fields stay null. Exit multiples are assumptions, not current peer quotes.

Sensitivities cover growth, exit multiples, available FDs, remaining warrants, demand-debt calls, working capital, deposits, capex, subsidiary burn, tax claims, fees/dilution, hurdle rates and execution costs. Under 11% steady EBITDA margin and a 12-times exit multiple, the first rescue reverse-grid solution reaching 15% needs about 49.1% annual revenue growth. That is not a supported ordinary growth target. No entry range is published.

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text:
The strongest bear case is not disappearance of healthcare demand. It is cash-consuming growth purchased at a valuation that requires repeatable high returns. Tender acceptance or payment delays increase receivables and deposits; imported inventory and foreign exchange increase costs; competition compresses margins; demand lenders withdraw funds while capex and subsidiary burn continue. Discounted equity issuance or reduced operations can make the damage permanent. A lower terminal multiple and greater dilution compound the loss even with positive accounting profit.

The linked bear case assumes FY27 sales down 15%, then growth of −5%, 3%, 4%, 5% and 5%; EBITDA margins of 6.5–8%; ONWC of 35% declining to 32%; deposits of 9% declining to 8%; and an eight-times exit multiple. A separate stress calls ₹45.5977 crore demand debt during remaining FY27 instead of assuming rollover. These are conditional mechanisms, not assertions of actual default.

Counterevidence is meaningful: initial CMSS receipts were reportedly timely, ICRA upgraded the rating, substantial FDs exist, and localization could improve margins. A dated cash/funding bridge could reduce risk sharply. Thesis-break variables are inability to finance minimum operating cash, sustained uncollected tender receivables, loss of principal access or a material unresolved financial misstatement. An exact probability of permanent impairment is not estimable and is not invented.

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text:
A fivefold share-price outcome in five years requires 37.973% annual compounding; tenfold requires 58.489%. At current market capitalization, a 20-times terminal P/E and 8% net margin, an undiluted fivefold outcome requires about ₹2,810.30 crore revenue, and tenfold about ₹5,620.60 crore. These are arithmetic requirements, not targets, and exclude additional dilution.

That is roughly 12.1 or 24.2 times FY26 consolidated sales, requiring capacity, volume, collection, working capital and regulatory access far beyond verified evidence. A higher multiple lowers the necessary earnings but increases dependence on market pricing rather than operating returns. Rescue issuance and remaining warrants make these undiluted illustrations optimistic. The current record does not support a five-to-tenfold thesis or a compounder label simply because one year's revenue doubled.

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text:
1. Next consolidated results including Lifesenz: baseline FY26 revenue ₹231.8066 crore and core EBITDA ₹23.2238 crore. Flag growth without cash or unexplained perimeter changes.
2. Auditor-backed cash reconciliation: baseline reconstructed CFO −₹32.0417 crore and standalone issue-fee discrepancy ₹7.0119 crore. A material unresolved difference keeps G2 on Hold.
3. Dated accessible cash, FD encumbrance and bank limits: baseline cash/current accounts ₹5.2238 crore, FDs ₹38.6126 crore and demand debt ₹45.5977 crore. An unfunded operating floor keeps G3 on Hold.
4. CMSS final terms, accepted deliveries, receipts and completion extensions: the proposed 30 September date has passed; completion is not assumed.
5. Collections: receivables ₹67.3503 crore, over-six-month balances ₹7.0430 crore and over-three-year balances ₹1.2195 crore. Rising aged balances or write-offs without resolution worsen risk.
6. Operating security deposit releases: baseline ₹19.0451 crore; reconcile releases to contract milestones and guarantees.
7. Plant throughput, underlying approvals and project NOPAT/capital: no CAP score until returns can be attributed. January 2027 imaging localization remains a future milestone.
8. Acquisition valuation, consideration destination, the ₹5.0505 crore related loan and Lifesenz burn: no automatic recovery or value assumed.
9. Capital issuance: current 14,537,600 shares and 600,000 remaining warrants; track cash net of fees and diluted earnings, not headline fundraising.
10. Before implementation, obtain official BSE prices and a complete sixty-session tape, current restrictions, spreads, queues and lock-in-adjusted free float for an 800-share position. Unknown sessions stay unknown.

These are research checkpoints, not a claim that automated monitoring or trading has been activated.

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text:
Classification: Hold — unresolved; high impairment risk. BQS, GQS and IAS remain NS, preventing quality, growth and investment rankings. NS is not zero or a bottom ranking. Attractive end demand and rapid reported growth coexist with poor cash conversion and unverified current funding.

No ordinary entry price, allocation recommendation or buy/sell instruction follows. The ₹5 lakh lot-aware position is a standardized liquidity test only. A cheaper quote alone does not resolve G2, G3 or G4. Reassessment requires an auditor-backed cash bridge, accessible FD/bank confirmation, current group funding including Lifesenz, CMSS acceptance/collection, attributable plant returns and official liquidity evidence.

If those arrive, rebuild funded ordinary scenarios rather than relabeling a counterfactual rescue as the base investment case. Any favorable evidence must still meet the 15% nominal five-year hurdle after dilution. The limitations are substantive: there is no executable live quote, verified current bank balance or personalized portfolio assessment.

sections.title: Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text:
Issuer annual reports/results, the prospectus, CMSS filing, acquisition completion/release, IPO utilization and ICRA rationale anchor the analysis. Mirrors preserve issuer-authored material but are identified as mirrors. URLs, document dates, locators and SHA256 hashes accompany every source. Investor landing pages are pointers, not underlying approvals or documents.

The detailed 27 May acquisition annexure remained inaccessible with HTTP 403. The shareholding PDF was truncated at 1 MiB; it is not treated as the complete register. The official BSE daily archive request also returned 403. These failures do not prove an event did not occur. The 19 October quote is secondary. Sources accessed after cutoff may contain later information; only dated observations through cutoff are used.

March CRA liquidity is not October money. FD availability is unverified. Model assumptions include a 2% operating cash floor, separate working-capital/deposit ratios, capex, 25% cash tax, interest, demand-debt rollover, subsidiary burn and rescue fees/pricing. Net asset cash use is not known maintenance capex. Other income is consistently removed from core profit. Related loans, customs already paid, IPO residuals, operational property, acquisition outlays and old warrant deposits are never counted twice. Historical scopes and comparative versions stay separate.

Source-free backups retain financial extracts, models, results, source URLs/hashes and research prose, not raw issuer PDFs, HTML, OCR, images or personal identifiers. Isolated reproduction verifies arithmetic and artifact consistency, not fresh source authenticity. Fresh authentication requires retrieving the cited original bytes and comparing their hashes. Open questions are the evidence needed to resolve the gates, not blanks silently filled by assumptions.

evidence.claim: Exact issuer Hemant Surgical Industries Limited, CIN L 33110 MH 1989 PLC 051133, BSE 543916, ISIN INE 0 GYI 01028. Current interoperability master has 14,537,600 shares and 400-share lot.

evidence.claim: Standalone FY 21–26 revenue 59.7646→230.9871 crore gives 31.0475% CAGR; FY 23–26 CAGR 28.3878%. Annual growth was−3.24%, 0.87%, 116.84% in FY 24–26.
evidence.locator: Historical financial extracts and source financial statements.
evidence.contrary_or_limitation: Five-year pandemic base and latest tender step-change do not establish repeatable organic growth.

evidence.claim: FY 26 consolidated CFO reconstructed as 26.5033−54.1530−4.3920=−32.0417 crore. Cash change−32.0417−2.9746+69.3059=34.2896 reconciles 9.5469→43.8365.

evidence.claim: FY 24–26 standalone CFO/PAT−0.8733; FY 25–26 consolidated CFO/PAT−1.0449. FY 25 cash flow was recast to exclude borrowings from operating cash.

evidence.contrary_or_limitation: Positive FY 22/FY 23 cash flow and FY 25 recast CFO 4.631 provide counterevidence; expansion explains cash absorption, not recovery certainty.

evidence.claim: March 2026 consolidated debt 49.6648 crore contains demand borrowings 45.5977; cash 43.8365 includes 38.6126 FDs. Only 5.2238 cash/current accounts used as conservative opening available cash.
evidence.locator: PDF 122–126 borrowing/cash notes; CRA March 15 liquidity.
evidence.contrary_or_limitation: ICRA rated BBB Stable/A3+ and described 20 crore free liquidity March 15. Excluding all FDs is conservative uncertainty, not proof all are blocked.

evidence.claim: ONWC 26.0703→62.9115 and operating security deposits 1.4810→19.0451 crore explain large capital absorption. Average receivable days 69.07; closing-days proxy 106.05.
evidence.locator: Notes to receivables, loans/advances, other assets and current liabilities.
evidence.contrary_or_limitation: Current collection and tender-deposit releases are unknown; some supplier credit partly offsets capital need.

evidence.claim: Aggregate average ROIC proxy 15.1481% and incremental proxy 18.7241% are computable but mix tender working capital, deposits and plants. CAP remains NS.
evidence.locator: Book IC 79.3614→135.4016 and normalized core NOPAT bridge.
evidence.contrary_or_limitation: No project-level attributable incremental cash returns or utilization; aggregate ratio is not causal return evidence.

evidence.claim: March stock statement books 54.6958 versus bank 85.1564 crore; company explains 25% creditor margin methodology, FD/LC collateral offsets and an inventory clerical/human error.
evidence.locator: PDF 106/134 note 35; CARO PDF 83.
evidence.contrary_or_limitation: Auditors gave unmodified opinions and no reported fraud. A difference is not itself evidence of deliberate falsification.

evidence.claim: March Lifesenz loan 5.0505 crore lacked a specified repayment schedule; June 1 acquisition 66.66% completed. June 9 issuer release states 19.98 crore consideration.
evidence.locator: PDF 43–44/104–106; June 1 completion; June 9 release.
evidence.contrary_or_limitation: Company describes RP Ts as ordinary-course/arm’s-length; auditors say terms not prejudicial. Detailed May 27 valuation/transaction annexure was not retrieved. Loan recovery is not assumed.

evidence.claim: FY 26 new equity gross 51.18848 plus warrant deposits 10.33856 less issue fees 7.0119=54.51514 crore cash. May conversion increases shares 13,038,400→14,537,600; only remaining 75% top-up 22.15068 modeled.
evidence.locator: Equity/share premium notes; visually checked May disclosure PDF 2.
evidence.contrary_or_limitation: Deferred-tax credit 1.7648 in premium is not cash. Remaining 600,000 warrants could dilute further; initial 25% already received and not re-added.

evidence.claim: CMSS orders disclosed 19 February 2026 total 264.33 crore inclusive taxes. Final commercial terms and delivery were still under negotiation; proposed completion 30 September 2026 was conditional.
evidence.locator: Entire primary filing.
evidence.contrary_or_limitation: Interim supplies were being made in national interest and CRA observed timely initial receipts; final completion/acceptance not established by cutoff.

evidence.claim: Management says MediTape equipment commissioned and JMS Japan clinical validations completed; extrusion next FY and imaging localization target January 2027 remain forward-looking.
evidence.locator: PDF 12–14/72 strategy.
evidence.contrary_or_limitation: Company claims are not underlying regulatory approvals, acceptance certificates or evidence of plant-level returns. Aggregate tender wins 350 crore are not remaining executable backlog.

evidence.claim: JMS exclusive India relationships exceed 30 years, while ICRA says JMS-linked share 49% H 1 FY 26 versus 65% FY 20. Prospectus top 10 customers 40.65% FY 23.
evidence.locator: Prospectus PDF 28/187; ICRA business profile.
evidence.contrary_or_limitation: Distribution value-add, intense competition and unhedged FX constrain pricing power; current counterparty/segment concentration unavailable.

evidence.claim: Poly Medicure FY 26 manufacturing-led consolidated revenue 1875.2592 crore/operating EBITDA 457.7; Trivitron FY 25 provisional 489.8/3.9% margin; Skanray 9 MFY 25 margin−22.5%.
evidence.locator: Polymed PDF 32; CRA financial indicators.
evidence.contrary_or_limitation: Different periods, acquisitions, mix and leverage prevent direct valuation-multiple transplantation.

evidence.claim: 19 October secondary close 618.60 gives 899.295936 crore marketcap on current shares. ₹5 lakh buys 2 lots/800 shares/₹494,880 beforecosts. Official 60-session BSE tape is missing.
evidence.locator: exact ISIN master; 19 October secondary row; 60 NSE archive scan.
evidence.contrary_or_limitation: Official interop price range is not a closing quote. Missing NSE issuerrows are unknown BSE sessions, not zero trade days; 20-observation close× volume is not traded value.

evidence.claim: Gross asset cash presentation conflicts: annual purchases 9.3904/proceeds 7.26 versus results 1.6486/negative sale.4818. Both yield 2.1304 netuse.
evidence.locator: cash flow annual PDF 90/118; results PDF 7/14.
evidence.contrary_or_limitation: A common net cash use does not verify gross capex, maintenance split or disposal proceeds. FY 26 FCF after gross capex remains NS.

evidence.claim: Standalone printed financing 76.3834 omits 7.0119 issue cost relative to corrected 69.3715; printed net cash 41.3861 does not match 34.3742 BS increase.
evidence.locator: Annual PDF 90 visually inspected; equity fee note.
evidence.contrary_or_limitation: Consolidated cash reconciliation works with net proceeds. Unmodified opinion is preserved; a correction requires issuer/auditor explanation.

evidence.claim: Conditional funding models preserve 2% revenue operating cash, demand debt, cash taxes and capex; all conservative non-rescue paths breach. Fees and dilution are explicit in separate rescue cases.
evidence.locator: Embedded annual model/assumptions.
evidence.contrary_or_limitation: Not a claim of actual default or a confirmed need to raise this amount. FD availability, current collection and facility renewal could change paths materially.

evidence.claim: IPO 24.84 crore already substantially utilized by March 2025; unspent.6284 is not an additional October asset. Customs 3.5603 paid under protest is not a second debt payment.
evidence.locator: IPO utilization schedule; contingentliabilities note.
evidence.contrary_or_limitation: Recovery of customsdeposit is not assumed either; unresolved unpaid tax disputes.8862 stress-tested separately.
